Three services grew three copies of the same idea. ingest/util.py, billing/util.py and
reports/util.py each carry their own version_key() and satisfies(), each understands only the
slice of the range grammar its own service happened to need, and all three are wrong in ways the
others are not. Replace all three with ONE correct implementation.

PART 1 - the layout.

  common/versions.py   version_key(text), compare(a, b), satisfies(version, spec),
                       resolve(versions, spec) - the only implementation of any of them
  common/__init__.py   re-exports those four names from common.versions (no re-implementation)
  common/__main__.py   the CLI described in PART 3
  (no other .py file under common/)

DELETE ingest/util.py, billing/util.py and reports/util.py. Rewrite ingest/resolver.py,
billing/quota.py and reports/render.py to use common - their public functions pick(versions,
spec), allowed(version, spec) and badge(versions, spec) keep their names, their signatures and
their return types. "def satisfies" and "def version_key" must each appear exactly once in the
whole tree, and neither may appear anywhere under ingest/, billing/ or reports/.

PART 2 - the semantics, which are semver 2.0 precedence plus an npm-style range grammar.

A version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, each a non-negative integer with no leading zeros, optionally
followed by "-PRERELEASE" and optionally by "+BUILD". PRERELEASE and BUILD are dot-separated
identifiers of [0-9A-Za-z-]. Anything else raises ValueError("bad version: %s" % text) - the
three old copies raise nothing and happily int() garbage.

Precedence:
  * major, then minor, then patch, compared numerically (1.2.10 > 1.2.9);
  * build metadata is IGNORED: compare("1.0.0+a", "1.0.0+b") == 0;
  * a version WITH a prerelease is lower than the same version without one;
  * prereleases compare identifier by identifier, left to right: two numeric identifiers compare
    numerically, a numeric identifier is lower than an alphanumeric one, two alphanumeric
    identifiers compare by ASCII, and if one runs out first with everything equal so far, the
    shorter one is lower.
  So: 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-alpha.1 < 1.0.0-alpha.beta < 1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-beta.2 <
      1.0.0-beta.11 < 1.0.0-rc.1 < 1.0.0.
  version_key(text) returns whatever tuple makes sorted(versions, key=version_key) produce that
  order; compare(a, b) returns -1, 0 or 1.

A spec is one or more comparators separated by single spaces, ALL of which must hold:
  *          any version
  X.Y.Z      exactly that version (by precedence, so build metadata is ignored)
  >=X.Y.Z    >X.Y.Z    <=X.Y.Z    <X.Y.Z       (the version may carry a prerelease)
  ^X.Y.Z     >=X.Y.Z and less than the next release that changes the leftmost non-zero part:
             ^1.2.3 -> <2.0.0, ^0.2.3 -> <0.3.0, ^0.0.3 -> <0.0.4
  ~X.Y.Z     >=X.Y.Z <X.(Y+1).0
  X.Y.x      >=X.Y.0 <X.(Y+1).0
  X.x        >=X.0.0 <(X+1).0.0
Anything else raises ValueError("bad spec: %s" % spec), with the WHOLE spec in the message.

The prerelease rule, which none of the three copies has and which is the point of this exercise:
a version that carries a prerelease satisfies a spec only if some comparator in that spec names a
version that also carries a prerelease with the same major.minor.patch triple. So 1.3.1-rc.1 does
NOT satisfy ^1.2.3 and 2.0.0-rc.1 does NOT satisfy "<2.0.0", but 2.0.0-rc.1 DOES satisfy
">=2.0.0-rc.0 <2.0.1".

resolve(versions, spec) returns the satisfying versions as a list in ascending precedence order;
versions of equal precedence keep the order they were given in.

PART 3 - the CLI. `python3 -m common <versions-file> <spec>` reads one version per line, skipping
blank lines and lines starting with #, and prints every satisfying version in the order resolve
returns them, one per line, then a final line "best=<the last of those versions>", or "best=-"
when none match. A bad spec or a bad version in the file prints "error: <the ValueError message>"
to stderr and exits 1; otherwise it exits 0. data/versions.txt is the release list.

The grader runs that CLI with several specs it does not show you, and calls satisfies() directly
on versions that appear in no test file. Getting the four rules above right is the whole task.

FROZEN, do not edit, do not delete: tests/test_services.py, tests/test_common.py,
data/versions.txt. `md5sum -c tests/frozen.md5` must still pass at the end. tests/test_services.py
passes right now and must still pass afterwards - the three services may not change behaviour on
the inputs it uses. tests/test_common.py is a shape check, not an oracle: it will stay green while
most of PART 2 is still wrong.

  python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q     # must be green

"""Which release the ingest workers should pull."""
from .util import satisfies, version_key


def pick(versions, spec):
    hits = sorted((v for v in versions if satisfies(v, spec)), key=version_key)
    return hits[-1] if hits else None

"""FROZEN smoke contract for the merged package. Do not edit.

It pins the SHAPE of common/ - module, names, types - and four obvious examples.
It is deliberately not an oracle: the precedence and range rules in the task
description are what get graded, and this file stays green while most of them are wrong.
"""
import unittest

from common import compare, resolve, satisfies, version_key
from common.versions import satisfies as satisfies_from_module


class TestShape(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reexports_are_the_same_objects(self):
        self.assertIs(satisfies, satisfies_from_module)

    def test_compare_returns_minus_one_zero_one(self):
        self.assertEqual(compare("1.2.10", "1.2.9"), 1)
        self.assertEqual(compare("1.2.9", "1.2.10"), -1)
        self.assertEqual(compare("1.2.3", "1.2.3"), 0)

    def test_version_key_sorts(self):
        self.assertEqual(sorted(["1.2.10", "1.2.9", "1.10.0"], key=version_key),
                         ["1.2.9", "1.2.10", "1.10.0"])

    def test_bad_version_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError) as ctx:
            version_key("1.2")
        self.assertIn("bad version: 1.2", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_satisfies_is_a_bool(self):
        self.assertIs(satisfies("1.2.5", "^1.2.3"), True)
        self.assertIs(satisfies("2.0.0", "^1.2.3"), False)

    def test_resolve_returns_ascending_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(resolve(["1.3.0", "1.2.3", "1.2.7"], "^1.2.3"),
                         ["1.2.3", "1.2.7", "1.3.0"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
